children: is scheduled to hold a key Investor Day event on September 23. The update should provide investors with an idea on how management plans to restore U.S. momentum while sustaining international growth. The durability of the new beverage platform, whose launches in the U.S., Canada, and Germany reportedly exceeded expectations, will also be closely watched.

After a year that has seen shares decline by more than 16%, investors will want greater clarity on development plans, capital allocation targets, franchisee economics, menu innovation strategy, and ways to monetize the digital business and leverage loyalty.
Deutsche Bank analyst Lauren Silberman expects the company to lay out select financial targets for 2027 and the longer term (2028-2030) and provide more details on the McDonald's

> NEXT strategy focused on its next phase of growth and productivity. "We believe the most anticipated area of focus is around MCD’s partnering contribution for the upcoming 10-year US remodel cycle and what that means for incremental capex over the next several years," wrote Silberman. However, she thinks investors are expecting some moderation in the unit growth outlook given global headwinds and potentially more capital constraints as the U.S. system approaches its reinvestment cycle and refranchising activity is expected to pick up. Silberman also expects a lot of focus on technology and recent U.S. trends.
RBC Capital Markets analyst Logan Reich highlighted that the McDonald's

Investor Day comes at a time when long-only interest in restaurant stocks remains depressed as macro pressures weigh on same-store sales growth. The firm thinks same-store sales growth needs to reaccelerate before investor interest ramps, which is not expected to be until the first quarter of 2027. Reich thinks the restaurant chain's plan on how to drive traffic will be a key area of focus for investors. "On beverages, we expect an update on the pace of international expansion, where the majority of global markets could get the platform soon," he added.

Morgan Stanley analyst Brian Harbour thinks the investor day will aim to generate excitement about the NEXT pillars, though the timing and cost discussion may mean the event is not an immediate positive catalyst or beneficial for numbers immediately. "We think investors will want to see proof points for some of the initiatives and see numbers start to move higher again, as do we to become outright constructive," he updated.
Wall Street analysts and Seeking Alpha analysts both have a consensus Buy rating on McDonald's
, while the Quant Rating is at Hold.
